# Browser support

<!-- Generated by packages/web-components/scripts/generate-support-matrix.mjs.
     Do not edit by hand. The matrix is derived from the Playwright projects
     that actually run, so a browser appears here only if a project launches it.
     Regenerate with `pnpm --filter @santaka-ui/web-components support-matrix`. -->

Two tiers, tested separately (ADR-014). **Baseline** gets full styling, motion,
and behavior. **Core** gets structure and behavior with degraded styling: a
feature Baseline uses freely is either avoided in component CSS or placed behind
`@supports`, so a Core browser keeps a working fallback.

| Tier | Meaning | Chromium (Chrome / Edge) | Firefox | WebKit (Safari) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | Full styling, motion, and behavior | 111 | 128 | 16.4 |
| Core | Structure and behavior; degraded styling | 90 | 121 | 15.4 |

The floors above are what each tier *guarantees*. What the suite launches is the
browser revision Playwright bundles, pinned by the lockfile:

| Engine | Playwright project | Bundled revision | Runs in CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chromium (Chrome / Edge) | `chromium-baseline` | `chromium-1248` | `browsers` job |
| Firefox | `firefox-baseline` | `firefox-1555` | `browsers` job |
| WebKit (Safari) | `webkit-baseline` | `webkit-2370` | `browsers` job |

## Test layers

Playwright also runs a `visual` project (ADR-019), which photographs example
sections rather than asserting behavior. It is a test layer, not a browser tier,
and it is deliberately excluded from the table above.
